svg.aria-label: Three layers of code review: the project's own linters, filtered to the lines this change touched and folded into the reviewer brief; the per-stack questions, asked only when triggered and answered before the push; and the affected contract tests actually running. Each layer states what it cannot catch.
svg.title: Three layers of code review: linters, questions, tests
svg.desc: Code review has three layers. First, the project declares its own linters; lumos only reads their output, keeps the warnings on lines this change touched, and folds them into the reviewer brief. It catches what a rule can express, not design-level problems. Second, the per-stack questions: only the ones this change triggers, each needing an answer before the push. It asks what linters have no rule for, but never judges whether the answer is right. Third, the affected contract tests actually run. That catches what was said right but built wrong; it cannot catch anything no test guards.

g.text: one change, going into code review
the project declares its own linters; lumos only reads their output
only warnings on lines this change actually touched
folded into the reviewer's brief — not dumped as a full report
can't catch: design-level problems — no rule expresses “this coroutine is on the wrong dispatcher”
what this stack should ask itself: 32 questions over six stacks, only the ones you touched
three answers: done (with evidence) / not applicable (with a reason) / not yet (linked issue)
one missing answer blocks the push, regardless of risk tier
can't catch: whether an answer is right — the tool checks evidence exists; reviewers argue the rest
the affected contract tests actually run before the push
red is red — another review record won't fix a failing test
the backstop: said right but built wrong is caught here, nowhere else
can't catch: anything no test guards — there, only the first two layers and you
three layers, three different classes of problem — drop one and nobody catches that class
